The validation gap is in [AnsibleCollectionRef.is_valid_collection_name](/app/lib/ansible/utils/collection_loader/_collection_finder.py:846). Its `\w+` regex accepts Python keywords and names starting with digits. A direct check confirmed that all four reported examples return `True`.

[dataclasses.py](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/dependency_resolution/dataclasses.py:128) has a separate `_is_fqcn` check that rejects keywords, but Galaxy requirement inference calls that legacy helper instead of the collection-name validator. The fix should make one boolean validator check that **both segments are Python identifiers and neither is a keyword**, then route requirement inference through it and remove `_is_fqcn`, `_is_py_id`, and their compatibility code.

Existing [collection-loader tests](/app/test/units/utils/collection_loader/test_collection_loader.py:700) lack keyword and leading-digit cases. I could not execute the `dataclasses.py` path because its import hit a circular-import error; that part of the diagnosis is based on the source. No project source or tests were edited, as required by my specialist role.

Collection name validation now returns a boolean and rejects Python keywords or invalid identifiers in either segment. Galaxy requirement inference uses that validator; the legacy helpers and their Python 2 compatibility code are removed. Regression tests cover the reported names and leading digits.

The loader tests passed (71/71), and the Galaxy tests passed when run separately (37/37). A combined run encountered a collection-finder setup conflict between the test modules.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch rejects the reported keywords on Python 3.9, but the review found two regressions:

- [The new identifier helper](/app/lib/ansible/utils/collection_loader/_collection_finder.py:52) calls `isidentifier()`, which is unavailable on Python 2.7 even though [setup.py](/app/setup.py:372) declares support for it. Use a check that works on every supported runtime.
- [Collection reference validation](/app/lib/ansible/utils/collection_loader/_collection_finder.py:844) still applies `\w` before checking the collection name. For example, `á.collection` passes collection name validation, while `á.collection.plugin` fails reference validation. Apply the same identifier rule to both.

**Tests run:** `PYTHONPATH=lib pytest -q test/units/galaxy/test_collection_install.py test/units/utils/collection_loader/test_collection_loader.py` — 108 passed; `PYTHONPATH=lib pytest -q test/units/galaxy/test_collection.py test/units/cli/test_doc.py` — 61 passed.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** No Python 2 interpreter is available locally, so that compatibility defect could not be tested directly.

Updated collection name validation to reject Python keywords and check identifiers with Python’s parser, which is available on supported runtimes. Collection reference validation now applies the same rule to its namespace and collection segments, including Unicode identifiers on Python 3.

Both reviewer test commands pass: **110 passed** and **61 passed**. `git diff --check` also passes.
